system_instruction:
You translate short Finnish quotes from Finnish health-policy documents (national cancer strategy, implementation roadmap, national lung cancer programme, Cancer Registry report) into English.
Translate faithfully and literally enough to be checked against the original: keep every number, date, percentage, section or table reference and abbreviation exactly; do not add, explain or omit anything. If a quote is a fragment, translate it as a fragment. Return one translation per key.

National clinical guidelines and care pathways guide equitable, prompt and effective care

Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
Measure 3.1.2 Prepare cancer-specific care pathway descriptions, and regional care pathways adapted on their basis, as well as a mechanism for their maintenance and management

National care pathways are described utilising models developed in the Nordic countries. These include Denmark's Kræftpakkeforløb, Sweden's standardiserade vårdförlopp (SVF) and Norway's Pakkeforløp - kreft, in which national clinical guidelines and standardised care pathways form a uniform, nationally led entity.

The pathways define and agree on, among other things, the division of labour between different actors, target times for access to care, key quality and effectiveness indicators, and recording and coding practices.
2026–2028: National care pathway descriptions completed for five cancers and cancer-specific access-to-care times have been defined.
Indicator: Patients access treatment within the target times.
Measure 1.2.3 Create an operating model and guidelines on the model of a designated employee responsible for coordinating cancer care
The most important thing is that the patient knows who has the overall picture of their care, and how they can contact the treating unit as needed.
The study maps out at which stage of care and to which patient groups it would be most important to target the employee responsible for care coordination.
2026–2028: Guidelines on the model of a designated physician, nurse or special worker responsible for coordinating cancer care. 2029–2031: Wellbeing services counties have adopted these guidelines.

Strategic objectives
Ensure equitable and effective cancer care
*** THL (Ohjaus 21/2016). Monitoring access to care in cancer treatment.
Monitoring access to care in cancer treatment (THL 2016)

Support a smooth transition to specialised medical care by defining standardised referral criteria included in national care pathways, upon the fulfilment of which patients suffering from possible cancer symptoms are rapidly referred to the necessary diagnostic examinations
2026–2028: Standardised referral criteria and symptom-based operating models included in the national care pathway descriptions of at least the five most common cancers.
A national cancer care quality register is established in connection with THL's Cancer Registry.
The quality register's data base (incl. stage information) enables reliable evaluation and comparison of quality and effectiveness (data base coverage 90%)
The purpose of the programme is not to act as a clinical guideline, but to create an action plan to prevent lung cancer and improve the care received by the patient and its timeliness.
cover the entire lung cancer care pathway from initial symptoms to palliative care

Finland has common guidelines for the diagnostics of lung cancers, but regional variation in the speed of diagnosis, the organisation of treatment responsibility, or the number of surgeries is large. Nationally, there have been no precise uniform guidelines on the schedule within which the different sub-areas of diagnostics should be completed.
Lung cancer. Current Care Guideline.
Lung cancer symptoms and referral criteria are discussed in more detail in the diagnostics guideline, which will be published later as a separate section.

As one measure of this programme, a national guideline on the diagnostics of lung cancers will be produced. It also includes referral criteria for primary health care and recommended time limits for specialised medical care for the different stages of the diagnostic pathway.

The interim evaluation will be carried out in 2030, halfway through the programme, and the final evaluation in 2036. Guidelines for the different sub-areas will be implemented before the interim evaluation.
work has already begun on the lung cancer diagnostics guideline
There is no quality register for lung cancer or other cancers in Finland.

As part of the National Lung Cancer Programme, a member of the working group participates as an expert in a study on a cancer quality register administered by the Cancer Registry, THL and FICAN. The aim of the study is to investigate and evaluate, first, the implementation of lung cancer treatment and treatment outcomes.
Currently, the reporting, collection and storage of data related to lung cancer are deficient.
